AI-Assisted Verification Coursebook
The AI-Assisted Verification Coursebook is a multilingual interactive learning platform designed to support journalists, students, educators, and verification practitioners in navigating AI-driven information environments.

Combining verification literacy, practical newsroom workflows, interactive multimedia learning, and comparative verification ecosystems, the coursebook explores how journalists can critically evaluate misinformation, synthetic media, and AI-assisted information while maintaining human editorial oversight.
The coursebook is structured around six interconnected modules, accessible through the module menu, and supports learning through interactive videos, podcast-style audio content, infographics, quizzes, flashcards, checklists, and real-world newsroom scenarios.

Rather than treating AI as an autonomous authority, the coursebook emphasizes human editorial oversight, critical evaluation, and ethical verification practices.
1
Misinformation, Disinformation & Malinformation
Information Disorder
Explore the differences between misinformation, disinformation, and malinformation, and understand how false or misleading information spreads across digital platforms. This section introduces the foundations of information disorder and explains why classification and verification are essential in modern journalism.
«Information disorder should not be treated as a single phenomenon because each category involves different actors, intentions, and verification responses»
Wardle & Derakhshan
Information Disorder: Toward an Interdisciplinary Framework for Research and Policy Making (2017)

2
Synthetic Media & Deepfakes
Learn how AI-generated images, videos, and audio are created, manipulated, and distributed online. This section explores deepfakes, cheapfakes, synthetic media risks, and practical verification strategies for journalists working in AI-driven information environments.
“These technologies enable face swapping, voice cloning, and synthetic video production.”
Abbas & Taeihagh, 2024 — Digital Policy, Regulation and Governance 
3
Virality and Algorithmic Amplification
Discover why false information spreads faster online and how algorithms, emotions, engagement systems, and AI-generated content influence digital visibility. This section examines the relationship between virality, platform dynamics, and verification challenges in modern media ecosystems.
“Falsehood diffused significantly farther, faster, deeper, and more broadly than the truth in all categories of information.”
Vosoughi, Roy, & Aral
The Spread of True and False News Online (Science, 2018)
This infographic illustrates how emotional engagement, algorithmic amplification, and AI-generated content contribute to the rapid spread of false information across digital platforms. It also highlights the differences between misinformation, disinformation, and malinformation within modern information ecosystems.
4
AI and the Verification Ecosystem
Examine how artificial intelligence transforms journalism, verification workflows, and global information ecosystems. This section introduces AI-assisted verification, newsroom integration, ethical challenges, and international verification initiatives, tools, and organizations shaping the future of trustworthy information.
The global verification ecosystem is composed of interconnected fact-checking networks, AI-assisted verification tools, newsroom verification desks, OSINT communities, media literacy initiatives, and research institutions working together to strengthen trustworthy information environments.

This section explores how journalists use verification platforms, collaborative standards, reverse image search systems, claim databases, AI-supported monitoring tools, and open-source investigation methods to identify, verify, and contextualize digital information in the age of AI-driven communication.

Global Framework

Global & European Verification Ecosystem

The global and European verification ecosystem is composed of networks, standards bodies, fact-checking organizations, AI-assisted tools, OSINT communities, newsroom verification desks, media literacy initiatives, and research reports. Together, these actors show that verification is not a single tool or institution, but a collaborative and constantly evolving professional infrastructure.

public

Global Standards

The IFCN and Poynter set the gold standard for transparency and methodology worldwide.

account_balance

EU Framework

EDMO and EFCSN provide institutional support and legislative harmony across Europe.

psychology

AI Integration

Next-gen verification leverages AI-assisted tools like Full Fact AI for monitoring at scale.

lightbulb Academic Context

The complexity of the verification ecosystem reflects the shift from isolated debunking to a holistic "defense-in-depth" strategy. By integrating technical tools (OSINT, AI) with ethical frameworks (IFCN Codes) and institutional oversight (EDMO), the network creates a resilient infrastructure capable of addressing disinformation at scale.
